ffl_flashpoint.name: Flashpoint
ffl_flashpoint.desc: The instant it catches — a ragged burn front with the first embers already thrown clear.

ffl_char_creep.name: Char Creep
ffl_char_creep.desc: Blackening crawls across the surface along the grain, carbon dendrites trailing behind it.

ffl_tinder_bloom.name: Tinder Bloom
ffl_tinder_bloom.desc: Dry fibre catching all at once: hundreds of thin bright threads opening out of a rough front.

ffl_match_head.name: Match Head
ffl_match_head.desc: Crimson strontium flare — the chemical head burning ahead of the wood.

ffl_smoulder_bed.name: Smoulder Bed
ffl_smoulder_bed.desc: Heat travelling underground through a packed bed, glowing only where it found air.

ffl_fuse_line.name: Fuse Line
ffl_fuse_line.desc: Lilac potassium running along a powder trail, spitting as it goes.

ffl_kindle_lattice.name: Kindle Lattice
ffl_kindle_lattice.desc: Stacked kindling seen from above, each cell lighting on its own schedule.

ffl_spark_shower.name: Spark Shower
ffl_spark_shower.desc: White-gold thermite spray, every particle burning out along its own arc.

ffl_ember_catch.name: Ember Catch
ffl_ember_catch.desc: A landed ember taking hold — bright cores spreading into the cold bed around them.

ffl_pilot_ring.name: Pilot Ring
ffl_pilot_ring.desc: The blue pilot crown: cool methane braids holding a steady standing flame.

ffl_autoignition.name: Autoignition
ffl_autoignition.desc: No spark needed — the whole surface reaches temperature at once and creases as it goes.

ffl_firebrand_scatter.name: Firebrand Scatter
ffl_firebrand_scatter.desc: Burning debris carried downwind, each brand starting a new small front where it lands.

ffl_scorch_front.name: Scorch Front
ffl_scorch_front.desc: The dark boundary between what has burned and what has not, creased by its own heat.

ffl_ignition_delay.name: Ignition Delay
ffl_ignition_delay.desc: Fuel and air mixed but not yet lit — pale sulfur blue drifting over a cold bed.

ffl_touchpaper.name: Touchpaper
ffl_touchpaper.desc: Amber sodium creeping through treated paper along every fibre at once.

ffl_diffusion_sheet.name: Diffusion Sheet
ffl_diffusion_sheet.desc: Where fuel meets air the burn is a SURFACE, not a volume — a shoal of thin reaction sheets.

ffl_wrinkled_front.name: Wrinkled Front
ffl_wrinkled_front.desc: Michelson-Sivashinsky cusping: a flame front unstable to its own curvature, creasing everywhere.

ffl_darrieus_cell.name: Darrieus Cell
ffl_darrieus_cell.desc: Darrieus-Landau cellular instability — a premixed flame breaking into its own honeycomb.

ffl_turbulent_braid.name: Turbulent Braid
ffl_turbulent_braid.desc: Shear at the flame edge rolling into braid after braid, never one big billow.

ffl_flamelet_storm.name: Flamelet Storm
ffl_flamelet_storm.desc: Turbulence tears the front into thousands of independent flamelets, each burning on its own.

ffl_buoyant_fingers.name: Buoyant Fingers
ffl_buoyant_fingers.desc: Rayleigh-Taylor: hot gas punching up through cold in a hundred small fingers.

ffl_shear_tongue.name: Shear Tongue
ffl_shear_tongue.desc: Amber tongues leaning off a shear layer, licked into ribbons by the crossflow.

ffl_pool_puff.name: Pool Puff
ffl_pool_puff.desc: A pool fire breathing — the periodic puff of a buoyant plume, resolved into cells.

ffl_candle_cone.name: Candle Cone
ffl_candle_cone.desc: The quiet laminar burn of a wick, all its structure in the fine creases of the sheath.

ffl_blowtorch.name: Blowtorch
ffl_blowtorch.desc: Forced-air blue: the flame stretched thin and fast, streaks running with the jet.

ffl_backdraft_wrinkle.name: Backdraft Wrinkle
ffl_backdraft_wrinkle.desc: Starved, then fed — the front folds back on itself the instant the air arrives.

ffl_fire_whirl_grain.name: Fire Whirl Grain
ffl_fire_whirl_grain.desc: Rotation stretches every filament into the same handedness — a whirl written in grain, not in a spiral.

ffl_laminar_ladder.name: Laminar Ladder
ffl_laminar_ladder.desc: An orderly premixed burn: rungs of blue at a fixed spacing, cells filling between them.

ffl_crown_fire.name: Crown Fire
ffl_crown_fire.desc: Fire in the canopy — it stops running along the ground and starts leaping between crowns.

ffl_stoichiometric_seam.name: Stoichiometric Seam
ffl_stoichiometric_seam.desc: Emerald boron marking the exact ratio line where fuel and oxidiser are perfectly matched.

ffl_arc_filament.name: Arc Filament
ffl_arc_filament.desc: Past burning: an ionised channel that carries current, not fuel.

ffl_ionised_braid.name: Ionised Braid
ffl_ionised_braid.desc: Current and field braiding around each other down the length of the column.

ffl_magnetised_jet.name: Magnetised Jet
ffl_magnetised_jet.desc: Copper-blue plasma collimated by its own magnetic field into a single hard direction.

ffl_corona_grain.name: Corona Grain
ffl_corona_grain.desc: The violet haze at the edge of a charged surface, grainy right down to the pixel.

ffl_streamer_web.name: Streamer Web
ffl_streamer_web.desc: Streamers branching ahead of the main channel, each looking for the easiest path.

ffl_townsend_cascade.name: Townsend Cascade
ffl_townsend_cascade.desc: One electron becomes two, two become four — avalanche until the whole gap conducts.

ffl_pinch_instability.name: Pinch Instability
ffl_pinch_instability.desc: The column squeezes itself, necks, and tears — sausage instability written across the surface.

ffl_cathode_spot.name: Cathode Spot
ffl_cathode_spot.desc: Blinding white attachment points skittering across the electrode surface.

ffl_glow_discharge.name: Glow Discharge
ffl_glow_discharge.desc: Low pressure, low current — an even green glow with visible striations in it.

ffl_lichtenberg_burn.name: Lichtenberg Burn
ffl_lichtenberg_burn.desc: The fractal scar a discharge leaves behind, branching at every scale it can find.

ffl_plasma_sheath.name: Plasma Sheath
ffl_plasma_sheath.desc: The thin charged skin that forms wherever plasma meets a solid wall.

ffl_spectral_line.name: Spectral Line
ffl_spectral_line.desc: Apple-green barium emitting on one narrow line and nothing else.

ffl_electron_avalanche.name: Electron Avalanche
ffl_electron_avalanche.desc: Every track a carrier multiplying as it runs; the surface saturates from the leading edge back.

ffl_tokamak_ripple.name: Tokamak Ripple
ffl_tokamak_ripple.desc: Confined and stable — nested flux surfaces rippling in step.

ffl_aurora_column.name: Aurora Column
ffl_aurora_column.desc: Charged particles following field lines down — curtains of green standing on end.

ffl_pahoehoe_skin.name: Pahoehoe Skin
ffl_pahoehoe_skin.desc: The ropy skin of slow lava, folding over itself as the crust drags on the flow beneath.

ffl_slag_crust.name: Slag Crust
ffl_slag_crust.desc: Waste glass floating on the melt, cracked into plates with heat still showing through the seams.

ffl_lava_cell.name: Lava Cell
ffl_lava_cell.desc: Convection cells on an open melt — dark crust above, orange shear at every boundary.

ffl_quench_craze.name: Quench Craze
ffl_quench_craze.desc: Hot glass into cold water: a craze network that keeps sub-dividing its own biggest fragments.

ffl_vitrified_glaze.name: Vitrified Glaze
ffl_vitrified_glaze.desc: Ash fused to a glassy skin, then cooled until it crazed — kiln chemistry, not paint.

ffl_weld_pool.name: Weld Pool
ffl_weld_pool.desc: The frozen ripple record of a moving arc, each crescent one pulse of the weld.

ffl_molten_drip.name: Molten Drip
ffl_molten_drip.desc: White-hot metal running and freezing on the way down, in hundreds of fine rivulets.

ffl_crucible_skin.name: Crucible Skin
ffl_crucible_skin.desc: Oxide plates lifting off the wall of a crucible, each curled at the edge and lit underneath.

ffl_basalt_column.name: Basalt Column
ffl_basalt_column.desc: Cooling contraction cracking a flow into columns — the same physics as mud, at 1200 degrees.

ffl_obsidian_chill.name: Obsidian Chill
ffl_obsidian_chill.desc: Cooled too fast to crystallise: black glass with conchoidal fracture running through it.

ffl_foundry_spatter.name: Foundry Spatter
ffl_foundry_spatter.desc: Thrown metal freezing where it lands, pocking the plate it lands on.

ffl_tuyere_glow.name: Tuyere Glow
ffl_tuyere_glow.desc: Looking in through the blast port: the hottest zone of the furnace, seen through moving gas.

ffl_slumped_glass.name: Slumped Glass
ffl_slumped_glass.desc: Glass gone soft and taken the shape it was resting on, the flow still legible in the surface.

ffl_magma_vesicle.name: Magma Vesicle
ffl_magma_vesicle.desc: Gas coming out of solution — bubbles frozen at the instant the melt stopped moving.

ffl_ropy_flow.name: Ropy Flow
ffl_ropy_flow.desc: Fast pahoehoe: the skin dragged into tight parallel ropes by the flow under it.

ffl_ember_bed.name: Ember Bed
ffl_ember_bed.desc: What is left when the flame goes: a bed that is all heat and no light, breathing where air reaches it.

ffl_ash_fall.name: Ash Fall
ffl_ash_fall.desc: Fine grey settling out of the air and building up wherever the wind lets it.

ffl_soot_bloom.name: Soot Bloom
ffl_soot_bloom.desc: Carbon inception: dendrites branching out of nothing, the deadest material in the catalog.

ffl_char_scale.name: Char Scale
ffl_char_scale.desc: Burnt skin gone to alligator scale, every plate lifted a little at its edge.

ffl_cinder_lattice.name: Cinder Lattice
ffl_cinder_lattice.desc: The connected skeleton that survived — only the paths that stayed lit are still there.

ffl_fly_ash.name: Fly Ash
ffl_fly_ash.desc: Spent particles too light to fall, drifting until they cool to nothing.

ffl_coke_cell.name: Coke Cell
ffl_coke_cell.desc: Coal cooked without air until only the carbon cell wall is left standing.

ffl_clinker_crust.name: Clinker Crust
ffl_clinker_crust.desc: Fused ash that went hard and vitreous in the grate — the stuff you have to break out.

ffl_ash_glaze.name: Ash Glaze
ffl_ash_glaze.desc: Wood ash melted onto the pot by its own kiln and crazed as it cooled.

ffl_dying_coal.name: Dying Coal
ffl_dying_coal.desc: The last of the heat retreating into the middle of each lump.

ffl_grey_front.name: Grey Front
ffl_grey_front.desc: Ash advancing over ember — the moment a fire stops being orange.

ffl_retained_heat.name: Retained Heat
ffl_retained_heat.desc: Cold on the outside, still dangerous in the core; convection barely moving above it.

ffl_powder_burn.name: Powder Burn
ffl_powder_burn.desc: Residue of a fast burn: scorched powder with a few grains that never went off.

ffl_spall_field.name: Spall Field
ffl_spall_field.desc: Thermal shock popping flakes off the surface, each leaving a paler crater.

ffl_cold_ash.name: Cold Ash
ffl_cold_ash.desc: Completely out. Fine grey powder holding the shape of what it used to be.
